title: L3Harris completes 60 Wolf Pack flight tests spanning strike and electronic warfare capabilities
source_used: Defence Industry Europe (relaying an L3Harris statement)
key_facts: L3Harris Technologies said its Wolf Pack launched-effects vehicles completed their 60th flight test earlier this year.
Tests covered launches from fixed-wing aircraft (13), helicopters (3) and ground platforms (44).
The portfolio is Red Wolf, intended for kinetic strikes, and Green Wolf, which carries an electronic warfare payload; both use a common air vehicle.
Across the 60 flights the vehicles supported 10 radios, six electronic warfare payloads, one seeker and two autonomy engines.
Software supports real-time collaboration, dynamic retargeting and coordinated autonomous swarming.
L3Harris cited geopolitical events as a driver of demand and said the US Department of War is accelerating investment in launched effects.
The company says it has delivered more than 1,200 released effects over 20 years of air vehicle production.
quote_evidence: L3Harris Technologies said its Wolf Pack launched-effects vehicles completed their 60th flight test earlier this year.
The company recorded 13 fixed-wing aircraft launches, three rotary-wing aircraft launches and 44 ground launches.
With autonomy, those capabilities can also operate together in a cooperative swarm.
why_it_matters_hint: Military buyers are being offered launchable autonomous craft for strike and electronic warfare that can work in swarms.
notes: Company-sourced; no independent confirmation, no operational use, order or price stated. Tests are undated. The page also carries unrelated defence headlines, not used.
